A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuronLens research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation-distribution analyses, saliency comparisons, concept-erasure experiments, and masking ablations across language models and classification datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original language-capability evaluations, intervention comparisons, range-width sensitivity results, and layerwise activation analyses.

M1.justification: v2 expands range-gated zeroing into a framework supporting dampening and mean replacement, and introduces adaptive dampening based on distance from the class-conditional activation mean (Appendix D.3). This substantially extends intervention behavior while retaining the original saliency selection and activation-range estimator.

E1.justification: The five classification datasets are retained. v2 adds Wikipedia next-token prediction and MMLU knowledge evaluation to measure capabilities after concept erasure, extending evaluation beyond classification-label preservation (Appendix C).

E2.justification: Appendix D adds evaluated static dampening, attributed to Suau et al. (2024), and mean replacement, attributed to Suau et al. (2021), alongside their range-restricted counterparts and the adaptive variant. The original Probeless, Probe, and Max comparison remains in v2 Tables 1 and 8.

E3.justification: New protocols include zero-shot MMLU accuracy, Wikipedia perplexity after intervention, alternative interventions with 30% of Llama neurons selected, and a tau sweep from 0.3 to 4.5. The exact static dampening factor is unresolved: Table 5 states 0.125, whereas Appendix D.1's discussion states 0.5.

E4.justification: v2 adds range-width sensitivity testing, comparisons of intervention strategies, and statistical and visual activation-distribution analyses across all 12 GPT-2 layers (Appendices D, H, and I). The earlier neuron-percentage analysis and Emotions layer-masking ablation are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions use trimmed means and the same practical-normality assessment. Neither reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty estimates for intervention performance. Applying existing distribution statistics to additional layers does not change the reporting practice.

E6.justification: The matched original classification and layer-masking tables retain their numerical values. v2 adds substantial results in Tables 4–7, 9–10 and Figures 7–18. For example, new Table 4 reports Wikipedia perplexity after IMDB erasure of 10.990 under neuron masking versus 7.550 under range masking, from a 7.007 baseline.

T1.justification: Appendix D.3 introduces the mathematical definition a(x) = beta|x−mu|/(2.5 sigma), with corresponding center and boundary behavior for adaptive dampening. The original range estimator and concept definitions remain; no substantial theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: v2 replaces claims that activation ranges are the proven 'true fundamental unit' with an empirical claim that they offer a finer unit of interpretation. It also adds a first-comprehensive-spectrum-study novelty claim and a claim of up to sevenfold reduced interference with general LLM capabilities.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations connecting layer depth to semantic separation, range width to the erasure–interference tradeoff, and adaptive suppression to preservation of contextual information and general capabilities. It also proposes future polysemanticity measurement and SAE diagnostics. The existing overlap, fixed-tau, and layer-selection limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies CLS versus class-prediction token extraction, intervention on the residual stream, and RTX 3090 hardware with 24 GB VRAM and 64 GB RAM. It also documents adaptive beta and Wikipedia-based replacement-mean estimation. These disclosures do not establish changes to the retained training procedures.

R1.justification: v2 credits Gaussian-activation observations to Gurnee et al. (2024), adds intervention, steering, and representation-probing references, and removes logit-lens and tuned-lens coverage. These refine the literature positioning while preserving the central motivation for range-based attribution.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, results discussion, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting. Metrics move into the preliminaries, the impact statement moves to the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized around capabilities, interventions, implementation, sensitivity, and layer analyses.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to predominantly one column and extensively relocates and resizes displays. It summarizes Table 1 while retaining its detailed rows in Table 8, moves the AG-News comparison to Table 13, and adds intervention/sensitivity tables and twelve layerwise figures.

improvement.justification: The new Wikipedia/MMLU checks address v1's lack of evidence about collateral damage beyond classification labels. Alternative-intervention, tau-sensitivity, and layerwise analyses substantially strengthen validation, while the central interpretability claim becomes more appropriately qualified. These gains outweigh the new dampening-factor inconsistency and overly broad adaptive-superiority statements, although those issues still limit reproducibility and confidence in the adaptive variant.
